findings.location: sections/50-comparison.tex l.86-87 (the A/B summary sentence) and l.50-51 (third column of the row 'Differences among its witnesses')
findings.problem: Two precision points in the repaired comparison. (a) 'The first reading speaks of a dominion received, the second of a dominion that needs nothing given.' The phrase the sentence rests on is Chrysostom's 'sufficient for itself, needing nothing' (Hom. in Io. 83.4, quoted at 30 l.80-83), and in his homily it means that Christ's kingdom needs no servants. Read against 'a dominion received', the sentence suggests that the second reading denies that the dominion is given. The second reading holds no such thing: its Offertory 'gives the nations as inheritance' (30 l.233-236), and the comparison itself says, three sentences later, that 'either birth serves it'. So the summary sentence overstates the difference between two compatible emphases. (b) In the new row the first two cells state the positions (for example 'Hilary reads the resurrection, Augustine the eternal generation'). The third cell names only the topics: 'Hilary and Augustine on the Son's subjection; Augustine and Bellarmine on when he sits'. A reader of the table cannot learn from it what the differences are.
findings.required_result: (a) Say what the second reading's power needs nothing of: for example, a power from above that needs no servants and takes nothing from this world. The contrast should be a dominion received as man against a power whose origin and means are not from the world. (b) State the third reading's two differences briefly: on the subjection, the servant's form subject (Augustine) or the body translated so that he becomes 'God only' (Hilary); on the session, begun now in the saints and continuing (Augustine) or after the judgment (Bellarmine).

findings.location: sections/20-lamb-receives-the-kingdom.tex l.98-100 (Aquinas, Super Ps. 2 n. 6); sections/30-kingdom-not-from-hence.tex l.126-130 (Augustine, En. in Ps. 2.9)
findings.problem: Two small source-precision points, in passages unchanged since iteration 0 but inside files under review. (a) The study quotes 'et hoc exemplum voluit ostendere per Christum'. The cited text (Corpus Thomisticum page cps02, matched to the registered artifact ...cps02-html-73a0a0c2) reads 'hoc exemplum voluit ostendere per Christum', without 'et'. The insertion comes from research/scope.md l.641. (b) 'On the second psalm he speaks to the kings directly: "now that I am set as King, be ye not sad, kings of the earth ..."' (2.9). In the tracked NPNF I.8 text Augustine introduces those words as an alternative: 'It can also be taken thus'. His first reading of 'And now understand, ye kings' (2.8) takes the kings as the spiritual, 'able now to govern all that is servile and brutish in you'. The second reading's case for the kings' office rests chiefly on Letter 185 and En. in Ps. 71.13-14, so the effect is small. Even so, the sentence states as Augustine's reading what he offers as a possible one.
findings.required_result: (a) Quote Aquinas exactly: 'hoc exemplum voluit ostendere per Christum'. (b) Mark the 2.9 address as the reading Augustine also allows, for example 'he also allows the verse to be spoken to the kings of the earth: ...', and keep the quotation.

summary: Artifact: the expansive study main.tex of liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/f01-christ-the-king (Claude, 1962 Missal, F01), built in this reviewer's scratch directory: 33 physical pages, byte-identical to the author proof (SHA-256 0af471dc...699f), all fonts embedded, no overfull, undefined-reference or rerun warning; all twenty review-input hashes matched. Read the whole study, the moved files closely (10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 80, generation-metadata, production-review), and a sentence diff against the iteration-0 text. Standing findings: STU-001 is repaired. Each of its seven instances now states the material, and two more of the same kind were also rewritten. No new process narration of that class was found. STU-002 is repaired: the comparison now places the A/B difference at the Gospel, assigns the Jn 18:37 split to the second reading's own witnesses and to the first reading's objection, gives the third reading's real objection (Cyril of Jerusalem, Jerome), describes the cross per reading, and counts Hilary in all three. Advisories STU-003, STU-004 and STU-006 are cleared, and so are STU-007 (a) and (b). STU-005 is partly cleared and STU-007 (c) waits on research. Checked evidence, every copy hash-matched to the registered artifact or to the digest recorded in scope.md: Hilary, Tract. in Ps. 2.30-33 (CSEL 22 OCR 6b39d974..., matched); Aquinas, Super Ps. 2 nn. 5-6, 9 (cps02 73a0a0c2...) and Super Io. 18 lect. 6 (ed660055...); Augustine, Tract. in Io. 115.1-4 (tracked NPNF I.7), En. in Ps. 2.6-9, 28.10-11 and 71.13-14 (tracked NPNF I.8), Letter 185.19-20 (0e38b092...) and De Trin. I.8.15-17 and I.10.20-21 (e815d76f...); Chrysostom, Hom. in Io. 83.4 and 84.1 (c210c008..., 7d7b2893...) and Hom. in Col. 2-3; Hilary, De Trin. XI.39-40 (tracked NPNF II.9); Cyril of Jerusalem, Catech. 15.27-32 and note 1950 (tracked NPNF II.7); Jerome, In Dan. II on 7:13-18 (tracked PL 25); Cyril of Alexandria, In Io. XII (ec1fa9b7...); Bede on Apoc 1:5-6 and 5:5-7 in Marshall and in PL 93 (738afa82..., 36b5deeb...); Victorinus on Apoc 5 (5d316402...); Cassiodorus on Pss 2 and 71; Quas primas nn. 13, 16-19, 28 and 32 (f17b882f...); and every Schuster claim against The Sacramentary V pp. 200-204 (OCR 65192aa1...). Bellarmine was spot-checked on Pss 2 and 71. All are accurately quoted and attributed except the two small points in STU-009. Consequential-difficulty tests: (A) First reading. The difficulty is the Introit's accipere ... divinitatem and Postula a me (Ps 2:7-8), set against Chrysostom, Hom. in Io. 83.4, 'nothing which He received in addition'. At Tract. in Ps. 2.30 Hilary takes Acts 13:33 to make the decree the resurrection, and from Mt 28:18's data est he infers that the Son asked. At 2.31 he finds the asking in Jn 17:1-2 and the inheritance in the nations carried into the eternal kingdom. At 2.33 he says the servant is raised in deum ... ut esset quod fuerat ante. Aquinas, Super Ps. 2 nn. 5-6, gives two rights, hereditario et meritorio: voluit quod peteret quod sibi jure hereditario competebat. Outcome: pass. The prose teaches the question and the inferences, and now says once, as the reading's own application, what receiving divinitatem means. It states truly the narrower disagreement over the rule for texts of giving. (B) Second reading. The difficulty is Jn 18:36's de hoc mundo / hinc, set against Ps 71:11, Ps 2:10-11 and the Collect's subdantur. Tract. 115.2 distinguishes 'of' from 'in' and 'from hence' from 'here', and makes the kingdom those who believe (Col 1:13). Chrysostom, Hom. 83.4, says the empire is from above and that the world is not deprived of his providence. Aquinas, Super Io. 18 lect. 6, says non est hinc ... est tamen hic, quia ubique est, citing Wis 8:1, Ps 2:8 and Dan 7:14a. Letter 185.19 says the king serves God as man and as king, and Aquinas reports it on Ps 2 n. 9. Outcome: pass, with the En. in Ps. 2.9 precision in STU-009 (b). (C) Third reading. The difficulty is the Preface's traderet (1 Cor 15:24-28), set against the Alleluia's quae non auferetur and the Communion's Sedebit ... in aeternum. De Trin. I.8.16 makes the handing over the bringing of believers to contemplation, and I.10.21 makes the kingdom the faithful. Hilary, De Trin. XI.39, says he delivers not his power but us. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catech. 15.31-32, reads 'until' as setting no term, and Jerome, on Dan 7:14, writes quae nullo fine claudatur. Outcome: pass. Limits: the Greek of Basil and Theodoret was not re-read. Bellarmine was spot-checked only. Theodoret's Latin, Cassiodorus on Ps 28 and the Hippolytus scholia were not re-read in this iteration. Visual composition is left to the visual evaluation. Verdict: PASS. No blocking defect remains. Four advisories (STU-005 and STU-007 standing, partly cleared; STU-008 and STU-009 new) and one accepted finding (STU-010, the research record's comparison paragraph).
